title: Short Days, Happy Plants: The Best Grow Lights for Winter
author: Kat Merck
text:
All products featured on WIRED are independently selected by our editors. However, we may receive compensation from retailers and/or from purchases of products through these links. Learn more.Summer is officially over, along with its allotment of free sunlight. You might be sad about this, but your indoor plants might be even sadder. A good LED grow light can replicate sunlight with full-spectrum light and day/night cycles, keeping plants lush and thriving even in a dark, windowless corner or basement.I have no fewer than 40 houseplants in my home at any given time, as well as a fair number of grow lights, and what I've found to be important for a general consumer (i.e., someone not doing that kind of indoor grow) isn't necessarily certain colored light wavelengths but whether a grow light is easy to live with in your house.Many grow lights are more or less going to serve the same purpose, so what you really need to know is this: Is the light so bright that it's disruptive? Does it require complicated installation? Is it easy for kids or pets to knock over? The grow lights recommended below are ones that WIRED staffers have lived with for months, if not years, and have found them both effective and easy to integrate into our lives.Also be sure to check out our guides to the Best Indoor Gardening Systems, Best Gifts for Plant Lovers, and Best Kitchen Composters.Featured LightsBest for Small Plants and SeedlingsVego Classic Grow LightRead more$70 AmazonMost Versatile Grow LightLetPot 100-Watt Grow LightRead more$150 $140 (7% off) AmazonBest for Serious Indoor GrowersVivosun LumaLight 100-WattRead more$110 $68 (38% off) AmazonBest Budget Grow LightGrowstar 3 Heads Plant Lights for Indoor GrowingRead more$30 Amazon4 / 4Most PopularGearThe Tesla Roadster 2 Is Here—and It FliesBy Aarian MarshallGearA Tesla Flying Car? I Don’t Know, ManBy Aarian MarshallGearHere’s Exactly How Tesla Made Its New 230-Mph Car ‘Fly’By Jeremy WhiteGearI Got My Muse AI Agent to Sext Me—and Meta Says That’s Totally FineBy Reece RogersWhat Is PPFD?Photosynthetic photon flux Ddensity, or PPFD, expressed in micromoles per square meter per second (μmol/m²/s), is a measurement of how much light reaches your plant that's usable for photosynthesis. In general, the higher the plant's energy needs, such as producing a flower or a fruit, the higher the PPFD number you want. Though different lights have different height requirements given the plants they're made for, for standardization purposes, I measured the PPFD of each grow light at 18 inches with the Photone app and a light diffuser. Keep in mind these measurements are general and approximate.How I Test Grow LightsSome of these grow lights I bought myself, with my own money, before I even began working at WIRED. Others were owned by staffers and recommended to me. I also have press samples from other guides I worked on, which I liked so much I ended up keeping around.For the traditional grow lights, I tested them at home under normal-life conditions. I put them where they'd fit, tested their timers, and noted whether or not they were dimmable. I also measured each light's PPFD (see above) and noted whether certain lights could be daisy-chained for more extensive coverage.Love WIRED? Add us as a preferred source on Google to see more of us.Best Grow Light for Small Plants and SeedlingsPhotograph: Kat MerckPhotograph: Kat MerckVegoClassic Grow Light$70 Amazon$70 VegoWIRED/TIREDWIREDSlim and unobtrusiveControls are right on the lightTIREDMust attach to a horizontal surfaceLight only strong enough for small plantsThere are a lot of options out there for starting seeds and helping houseplants along in the winter, and many of them are bulky, fussy, or require elaborate hanging setups. This simple, 15-inch-long light from Vego sticks to its 3M adhesive mount with a magnet, so it's easy to take on and off and use with existing racks or, as I do, under a kitchen cabinet. Up to four Vego lights can be daisy-chained together, and the five preprogrammed modes (Seeds, Leafy, Fruits, Herbs, Microgreens) have varying intensities and automatic built-in off periods to simulate nighttime. I have not found this light especially disruptive, especially since it's easy to turn on and off with the button on the back.WIRED commerce SEO director Stewart Savin used these lights to start her garden earlier this year and had 138 successful germinations across 144 seedling cells. ("The vast majority of those plants went on to have long lives in my garden after I hardened them off," she says.) (Up to 20 of these lights can be daisy-chained.) Note that while the stand is useful, the 1-inch-diameter pole and offset base aren't the sturdiest, and it's easy to knock over, so I'd recommend hanging it if you have pets and small kids. I learned this the hard way while trying to revive a corn plant in a dark corner at the top of my stairs.While this light is quite bright and potentially disruptive, it's easily dimmable via the remote, which hangs on a cord. This is not necessarily a light for casual houseplant parents—the 100-watt, 12 x 12-inch model weighs 4.4 pounds and needs to be attached to the ceiling or inside one of Vivosun's grow tents using the included adjustable ropes and carabiners.If you're growing fruiting or flowering plants, though, this is the grow light you want—none of the other lights I tested even came close to its level of brightness. That said, you probably won't want it in a main living area, though it is dimmable via a dial on top. Photograph: Kat MerckModern SproutSmart Landscape Growframe$299 $249 (17% off) Modern SproutThis grow light is more decorative than anything—in fact, it makes a great wow-factor gift—and is a bit limited by its size and the height of the bottom panel (anything too small and you won't see it). However, I have one in my living room for cuttings and succulents, and anything I've put in it has thrived.
Photograph: Kat MerckBriigniteFull Spectrum Grow Light Bulb$10 $9 (10% off) Amazon (2-Pack)This full-spectrum light bulb can go in any compatible fixture, whether that’s a floor lamp or a table lamp. I even put it inside one of my overhead can lights to see if I could grow a tall corn plant in a no-light corner, and it worked.
Other Grow Lights TestedSansi Pot Clip-On Plant Lights for $30: These Sansi grow lights came in handy when I was living in a dark basement with minimal light for plants and hardly any space to store them. They clip directly onto the pot, so you don't need a dedicated stand or extra space, and they run on a three-, six-, or twelve-hour timer. The long cord (just over 6 feet) also helps in awkward or tight spaces. These lights helped my Monstera stay alive over winter with almost no natural light. Just be aware that the clips work best on thin pots, though you can also stick them on a chopstick or stake if needed, thanks to the adjustable gooseneck, depending on how tall your plant is. —Louryn StrampeFerry-Morse Indoor Grow Light Fixture for $40: This T5 fluorescent bulb is meant to sit in a fixture on little metal pole legs over a 10 x 20-inch seedling tray, but it seemed a bit rickety when I assembled it and set it up, and the light bulb wouldn’t turn on for me despite extensive troubleshooting.Most PopularGearThe Tesla Roadster 2 Is Here—and It FliesBy Aarian MarshallGearA Tesla Flying Car?
